title: Nivalis Nights dares to ask what if Cyberpunk 2077 met Dave the Diver and Stardew Valley? And for now at least I'm loving the answer
text:
As I throw open the windows on my first day in Nivalis, breathing in the city's neon-streaked air and watching the smog roil across the blackened sky, my government-mandated AI automata informs me the district is in lockdown and a serial killer's on the loose. Five hours later, I've become embroiled in a child trafficking plot (the good kind, apparently, seeing as I'm helping them get out); I've stumbled across an oil rig and befriended its city separatists; I've inadvertently struck up a romance with a CorpSec agent who's trying to shut down my noodle bar; and I've met a woman who writes new childhoods for condemned criminals, in the city's hope that implanting them will make 'em behave. All this and I've only grown a single onion. Nivalis Nights, it's fair to say, is not your average farm-life sim.

title: WoW: Forever Players Love It When Things Look Old
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever players have made their feelings about the game's visual style crystal clear: They love it when things look old.

It's a recurring theme in the Forever beta, where players have continually pushed back against updated high-definition character models and character portraits. While Forever is in many ways a new version of Blizzard's MMORPG, it's built with the spirit and foundation of WoW Classic in mind, even as it includes updated visuals and quality-of-life updates taken straight from modern WoW. One of those new features is an option to use modern WoW's updated playable character and non-enemy NPC models.

According to the WoW content creator Savix, who tested an early version of Forever before it was publicly announced, developer Blizzard didn't originally plan to include the ability to swap between standard or high-def character models, instead only using HD models. The testers, many of them streamers and content creators from within the WoW Classic community, stressed how important it was to include an option for the game's original character models.

Blizzard thankfully listened, but every other instance of updated character models have been met with similar distaste from among the MMO's community. Whether it was intentional or by mistake, a quilboar boss was found to be using its modern WoW model and was met with backlash from players. It didn't take long for Blizzard to return the enemy back to how it looked in WoW Classic. 

It's a similar story with the game's character creation portraits. For much of the beta, the Forever character-creation screen used HD portraits taken from modern WoW, to the disappointment of the community. Earlier this week that finally changed, with the game now using WoW's original character-creation portraits.

Blizzard seems to have gotten the message. Currently, the game's new playable Skyborne elf race only has HD models. That, too, sounds like it will soon change. In a comment attached to a video exploring Skyborne lore and abilities, Blizzard said to "stay tuned regarding Skyborne models," seemingly implying standard-definition versions of the Skyborne are on the way. 

Even with these options, some players want more. Forever's user interface is a fascinating combination of old and new--cleaner and more streamlined similar to modern WoW, but inspired in many ways by WoW Classic. Currently, there's not a toggle option to swap between Forever's updated UI and WoW's original interface. For those who want the UI as it was 20 years ago, a player-made ClassicUI Forever add-on reverts many of Blizzard's changes to make everything from the game's action bars, spellbook, profession tab, character portraits, bags, and more look as they did in 2004. 

I expect this push and pull to continue. WoW content creators have debated the clash between old and new found in Forever's art style, with many calling on Blizzard to pick a lane. For what seems like the majority of the Forever community, the answer is loud and clear--the older looking the better. 

WoW: Forever's beta runs through October 21, with Forever's full launch coming November 4. A recent RMT controversy in the Forever beta saw Blizzard put its foot down when it comes to illegal gold buying. Meanwhile, Blizzard is asking players in a survey for their opinions on 11 potential new classes that could be added to Forever in the future.

title: New Details Revealed For GTA 6’s Jason And Lucia, Including “Physical Intimacy”
text:
New information has come to light about GTA 6, and specifically the partnership of its main characters, Jason and Lucia. In GTA 6, they are both partners in crime and lovers, and physical intimacy will be part of the experience, it seems.

Rockstar North's Rob Nelson said in an interview with IGN that physical intimacy is a "huge part" of a relationship, and that applies to GTA 6. Exactly how this may operate in GTA 6, however, remains a mystery. "It has to be done right," Nelson said.

"Like anything that we do, we have to iterate and try things and iterate on it until we figure out what feels right," he explained.

GTA 6's ESRB rating says the game will have nudity and strong sexual content, and IGN reported that when switching characters, it can switch to Jason's POV while he is naked and in the shower. An international rating for GTA 6 specifically mentions how the game will have "sex scenes."

The GTA series has had its fair share of sex-related controversy. One of gaming’s biggest controversies ever, the Hot Coffee surrounding GTA: San Andreas saw Rockstar owner Take-Two paying out money to settle suits related to a mod in GTA: San Andreas’ PC edition that unlocked an interactive sex minigame.

As of yet, there is no indication that any sex scenes in GTA 6 would be interactive.

Also in the interview, Nelson discussed Jason and Lucia's relationship generally, saying players will be able to "role-play" their relationship, and "it's amazing."

GTA 6's story is narratively structured around Jason and Lucia, and the two of them working together. They don't have to be a couple, though, and instead can be simply "partners in crime" who are not romantically involved.

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us," he said. "Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

Nelson went on to say GTA 6 will not give players "a particular gameplay benefit" if they have Jason and Lucia become lovers, however. But they will always have the benefit of "working together and having each other's back," he said.

"Whether they're romantically close or not doesn't change that. They will still work together. It's really about what you want for them, their story, and how it plays out. Whether you've nurtured the relationship or not will definitely have a bearing on how their story plays out," Nelson explained.

GTA 6 has a dedicated "relationship system" that is separate from a different gameplay system that tracks what sort of a criminal you are, Nelson said. Players can nurture the relationship between Jason and Lucia in the ways you would expect, including spending time together with things like kayaking and mini-golf. Or they can grow their relationship by robbing stores together.

"However players want to spend that time together, it will have a positive impact on the relationship," he said.

GTA 6's narrative setup has been likened to Bonnie and Clyde, the famous real-world criminal couple who met their end in a hail of gunfire. Many are wondering if both Jason and Lucia will make it out alive in GTA 6, or at the least, how their relationship may be tested. Another popular fan theory is that either Jason or Lucia is actually working with the Feds and will turn on the other at some point.

it won't be much longer until we find out, as GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: The Next Gears Of War Game Probably Won’t Need 7 Years To Cook
text:
After a lengthy hiatus, Gears of War returned this week to Xbox Series X|S and PC with a new adventure set during the cataclysmic events of Emergence Day. For fans of the series, it has been a long wait, as the previous entry in the series, Gears 5, was released all the way back in 2019. Will there be another seven-year stretch between new Gears games? Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition doesn't think so, as the new game lays the groundwork for a quicker turnaround for new potential chapters in the IP.

Speaking to the BBC, Coalition studio head Mike Crump said that E-Day provides a "great foundation" for future games, and he claimed that "the next game will not take nearly as long" to make. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control. For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that," Crump added in response to questions about the safety of the studio and its institutional knowledge during a period of mass layoffs at Xbox. "We've got a great team here. And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years. So there's definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience."

So far, The Coalition appears to have been spared the brunt of "Xbox reset" layoffs, but fears remain that the axe might swing their way now that Gears of War: E-Day has launched.

Recent changes at Xbox have seen several studios consolidated under Bethesda and Activision, and even Xbox's high-profile Halo series has not been spared. After being under the remit of Halo Studios for several years, a new team at Activision is now developing the next Halo game, rumored to be a new division within Call of Duty developer Sledgehammer Games.

The future of the Gears of War series likely rests with its commercial performance, but as an Xbox exclusive, there's only so much room for sales before you factor in its availability as a day-one Xbox Game Pass release and its launch during a crowded period on the gaming calendar. Crump sees things differently, believing the true measure of E-Day's success will be its ability to move the needle for Xbox and show what the gaming brand is capable of as it enters a new era, not just sales numbers.

"We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware," Crump said.

title: Google Playground Wants Everyone To Make AI Games, And Maybe Everyone Shouldn’t
text:
Stadia might be dead, but Google isn't giving up on gaming. The company has rolled out Playground, a platform built around AI that "lets you create, play, and share custom games." It's browser-based and labeled as an "experiment" to start. There's also Unity Spark support, which will offer more development options for people who catch the creator bug. 

Google's pitch claims that this new platform makes game creation more democratic by ending gatekeeping to development. The company states that Playground "lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts--no coding experience required." The platform also feels like the company's attempt at taking a piece of the Roblox pie--something that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly wants with Minecraft, too. 

However, the initial rollout feels pretty underwhelming. The most hilarious part of the Playground experience, so far, is realizing how misleading the cover art for games is after actually playing them. For example, we checked out Volcano Run. The key image shows a sports car racing around a road crumbling; meanwhile, the actual gameplay is a rudimentary rectangular motorcycle (we think) driving in a Tron-like environment. 

One of the Unity Spark highlights is called Horror Story, and the game starts with players following a ghost into a haunted house. How that ghost shuffles into the residence is one of the funnier animations we've witnessed in a game recently. 

The most promising experience we checked out was Steampunk Match, a match-3 puzzle game. Players need to create combos to stop a boiler from exploding. This game felt much better than others that attempted to take a swing at the action-RPG genre, such as Catacombs. 

If you are looking to make your own game for Playground, that opportunity is apparently rolling out to people "soon." However, Google says people can upgrade their Google One plan to get started immediately.

title: GTA 6 Won’t Make You “All-Powerful” Like GTA 5 Did
text:
Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has stated that GTA 6 won't make players "all-powerful" like they were in GTA 5 and the games that came before it. For GTA 6, this means NPCs in the world will have impulses of their own, and could come after you.

Speaking to IGN, Nelson said, "The world will act upon you as well as you acting upon the world." In previous GTA games, except for the police, the player was the only one with an "invisible arsenal hidden away," and everyone in the world would run away in terror. "This world in GTA 6 is not like that," he said.

Nelson went on to say that GTA 6's story, which follows the partners in crime and lovers Jason and Lucia, is about "criminals on the run." However, the game's narrative is such that they are incentized to "do what they need to do while not drawing unnecessary attention."

"So if you're doing things on a mission that you are required to do--or you’re robbing places, or somebody comes and messes with you and you have to deal with them by smacking them down or whatever--that’s all fair game," he said. "It's when you go beyond what is necessary on a consistent basis or you do completely unnecessary stuff consistently that you may start to sway your criminal profile in a certain direction. Maybe you care about that as a player, maybe you don't. There is no right or wrong way to play this."

Nelson said being "overpowered" as a character compared to everyone else except the cops "can be fun but not as fun" as a world in which other people may have "impulses of their own and act upon you."

"You are still powerful and capable, but you are not the only one capable of violence or the only one with weapons or the only crazy person out there," he said. "It makes the world far more unpredictable and interesting. It's something that we started doing in Red Dead Redemption 2, where you are not the only dangerous person in the world. There are gangs that will attack you, things that will happen to you. The world will act upon you. That happens here a lot, and then when it does, you have a decision to make. How do you want to deal with it?"

In GTA 6, the cops are getting upgrades, too. A new "heat" system means the police now know what the player looks like and what they're wearing, so even if players put on a hat or glasses, the cops still know who they are until they change clothes.

GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies. A recent report said the game might be available to stream in November, but that's apparently not the case.

title: State Of Decay 3 Was Announced Early To Keep Undead Labs On Microsoft’s Radar
text:
After leaving the Xbox Game Studios portfolio, State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs is now an independent, employee-owned studio. The developer had previously announced State of Decay 3 all the way back in 2020--partly to keep the project and the studio on Microsoft's radar--as the company embarked on an acquisition spree. Now one of several departures from Microsoft's gaming division following the bloody "Xbox reset" that has seen scores of jobs slashed throughout 2026, Undead Labs also had to cut staff as it entered a new era. But was there any behind-the-scenes drama that led to its exit from Xbox?

Speaking to The Game Business, studio boss Philip Holt said that ultimately, nothing went wrong. It was more a case of reading the room and making a proposal to Microsoft that the company accepted. "It was an accelerated period of time for Microsoft's divestiture," Holt explained. "We had a lot of interest. I also thought that because we were so close to being in revenue, the amount of capital that we needed to finish [State of Decay 3] was not an insurmountable amount that we couldn't go raise it ourselves. I knew other studios were doing management buyouts, so I submitted an offer for a management-led acquisition, and Microsoft thought that would be a good idea."

Holt also addressed why State of Decay 3 was originally announced so far in advance, as in the eight years that it was under the Xbox umbrella, it never released a single game--but it did drop 38 updates for the popular State of Decay 2. He explained that a small team had been working on the game since 2020--with development picking up a few years later--and that announcing the game so early helped the studio avoid being lost in the shuffle during Xbox's buying spree of publishers like Bethesda and Activision Blizzard.

"I didn’t think Microsoft was done being acquisitive, and I didn't think they'd continue buying small developers; I assumed they'd start buying big things. I was a little worried about getting swallowed up or divested before we had a chance to present to the world what we were working on. So, it was a bit of a marker on the table. I was saying, State of Decay 3, we're announcing it, the audience knows it’s in development, and here’s a trailer to demonstrate our vision."

State of Decay 3 will still launch day-one through Game Pass, and Holt credited the subscription service with helping the horror franchise reach 25 million players. He also said that becoming an independent studio allowed Undead Labs to focus on serving an audience and being profitable. "We need to make a profit, we need to be sustainable, we need to pay ourselves and our partners--and it is a goal. This is not a charity. But it’s not the number-one most important objective."

Undead Labs joins Double Fine and Compulsion Games as former Xbox studios, but the future of Hellblade and DmC: Devil May Cry developer Ninja Theory is looking grim. After deals to acquire the studio fell through, it looks like the studio will soon be shut down.

title: Skydance Is Merging Paramount And Warner Bros.’ Game Studios Into One Unit
text:
With Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in the bag, details on what this merger means for the Warner Bros. game division have finally been revealed. Warner Bros. Interactive will merge with the newly formed Paramount Games Studio, and it'll oversee projects based on Skydance's rich--and newly acquired-library of IP. That lineup includes Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, and Star Trek--and that's not even mentioning the treasure trove of DC Comics IP that the company now owns.

The new division will be overseen by Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, and one of the executives leading corporate strategy and development at the company. Driscoll had previously described video games as a "core pillar" of entertainment, alongside film and TV.

"We’re investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, film and direct-to-consumer: Games, experiences, consumer products, and publishing," Gordon wrote in a staff memo (via Variety). "These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage."

It's still unclear what the future plans are for the growing Skydance gaming division, or how hard it'll be hit by looming layoffs. This branch of Skydance will now be the home to some big WBI developers like Avalanche Software (Hogwarts Legacy), NetherRealm Studios (Mortal Kombat), Rocksteady Studios (Batman: Arkham Series and one Suicide Squad game I don't want to talk about), and TT Games (Various Lego games).

Former Activision CEO Bobby Kotick has also joined the board of directors, and Skydance is also producing the Call of Duty movie with Activision, which is scheduled to hit theaters in 2028.

title: Resident Evil Requiem DLC Could Further Rewrite One Of The Series’ Biggest Villains
text:
Resident Evil Requiem is one of this year's biggest hits, and Capcom plans to build on that success with new story DLC. While it hasn't yet revealed when it'll be out or what it's about, one of the game's writers, Haris Orkin, recently teased that the DLC will shed new light on Oswell E. Spencer, one of the biggest villains in the Resident Evil series.

"I think villains honestly are really fun to write, because I usually see every villain as a hero of their own story. So the villain is like in their mind they're a hero," Orkin said in an interview with the Distance Nerding podcast. I mean, Victor Gideon thinks he's going to save the world in Requiem. We have an arc for Spencer in Requiem. "Where you understand that more. And then in the DLC you will understand that even further. I probably shouldn't say that, but yeah."

Resident Evil Requiem spoilers below

Compared to his appearances in previous Resident Evil games, Oswell E. Spencer is more sympathetic, harboring genuine regret for his role in establishing the Umbrella Corporation, his research on the Progenitor Virus, and his ambitious goal of remaking the world with his bioweapons. As revealed in Requiem--and spoilers if you haven't played it yet--Spencer adopted a baby girl called Grace in 2001, and he successfully developed the powerful antiviral Elpis so that he could eliminate all Progenitor-based viral weapons, as part of his mission to atone for his sins.

That version of Spencer is narratively at odds with the version we see in Resident Evil 5, as before his death in 2006 at the hands of Albert Wesker, he was a bit of a bastard who apparently still harbored delusions of grandeur and had started work on a new virus to help him become immortal.

Then again, Capcom has been rewriting Resident Evil lore with its remakes, and this new version of Spencer is arguably more fascinating than a stereotypical mustache-twirling villain. While we don't know if Capcom plans to eventually make Resident Evil 5--one of the more controversial entries in the series--it'll be interesting to see if Spencer succumbs to his ambitions once again before Wesker finishes him off.

Since its launch, Capcom has updated Resident Evil Requiem with some photography tools and a new "Leon Must Die" mode. Resident Evil producer Jun Takeuchi also spoke about the meaning behind the title, adding to the confusion. Following the blockbuster success of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, the next entry in the video game series is out soon. The remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica launches in 2027.

title: GTA 6 Will Not Stream To PC Through Xbox, Despite Earlier Report
text:
PC players hoping to find a way to play GTA 6 when it launches on consoles next month must be feeling pretty disappointed, as Microsoft has clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be available to stream to PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming. The news follows an earlier report claiming Xbox had secured exclusive streaming rights to Rockstar's highly anticipated game.

The clarification came from Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, who addressed The Verge's report. Ball said the excitement surrounding GTA 6 and Xbox had resulted in some inaccurate reporting.

His full statement read, "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."

That means, sadly for PC players, that you shouldn't expect to fire up Xbox Cloud Gaming on November 19 and find yourself wandering around Vice City without a console.

The original report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had secured exclusive game-streaming rights for GTA 6, citing sources familiar with the company's plans. The report followed comments from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who apparently told employees that Microsoft was preparing to do something with GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing."

The report suggested the arrangement could have been significant for PC players, who as of yet don't know when they'll be able to get their hands on the game.

Rockstar has yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6, which is officially confirmed for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A streaming arrangement could have offered PC players a way to play the game at launch without waiting for the GTA 6 PC release date.

The confusion arrives at a pretty interesting time for Xbox Cloud Gaming. Microsoft is making significant changes to the service in November, including introducing a pay-as-you-go option and changing the amount of cloud gaming time available across Game Pass tiers.

title: Xbox Was At An “All Time Low,” But Is Now Growing Again CEO Says Without Providing Any Real Evidence
text:
During a town hall meeting today, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke to staff to help reassure them following mass layoffs and studio closures related to the "reset" of the business.

Windows Central reports that Sharma told staff that Xbox is "making the right decisions" and that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth," though she did not share any specifics. She added that Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft: Forever had "strong" starts, though she did not share any specifics.

Sharma said, "We've started to return to growth, more than 2 to 3 times what we were, and we expect that continue." She did not share any specifics about what "2 to 3 times" actually means, though.

Sharma also told staff that Xbox's "Gen-10" platform--AKA Project Helix--will be, as rumored, a "family of devices" because "there is no one device that fits all."

She said it's important for Xbox to have a "great console first," but there will also be options for players who are "on the go." Sharma went on to say that Microsoft will manufacture some of these devices, and others Microsoft will find partners for.

"So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this," she said.

Sharma didn't get into specifics about its next console or portable devices, but they're in the works amidst a very challenging time given the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. The global macroeconomic environment that has driven up oil prices has also rocked markets. Not only this, but in the US, the Federal Reserve recently raised rates, impacting borrowing costs with the effects trickling through various market categories, including gaming.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised Sharma for making such deep and extensive cuts at Xbox. This has so far included 1,600 layoffs in July, close to 300 more in September, and additional job losses to come. Microsoft also closed or divested of a number of studios, including Double Fine and Ninja Theory.

Some theorized Sharma was streamlining Xbox to make it more attractive to a prospective buyer, but she recently insisted that Xbox is not for sale. A lot of people don't believe her, though, pointing back to her comments about how "the plan's the plan until it's not the plan."

Beyond these moves, Sharma also oversaw a massive restructuring of the Xbox business that included Activision taking over the Halo series and Bethesda's remit expanding to also cover Obsidian.

title: Razer’s Wolverine V4 Controller Is Overkill For Most Gamers, And That’s The Point
text:
Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick sensor architecture.

One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracking with capacitive sensing.

Then there's the polling rate, which is absurdly high. For example, a DualSense Edge is capable of offering up to 1,000Hz (1 ms to 8 ms input latency), but the Wolverine V4 pushes that number up to 8,000Hz in both its wired and wireless configurations when used on PC, which, in theory, should put that on par with high-end esports mice and keyboards. This isn't the first Razer controller to feature an 8,000Hz polling rate, as the Wolverine V3 Pro was also equipped to reach those numbers.

Just don't expect to reach those levels on Xbox Series X|S, as hardware limitations cap the refresh rate at 250Hz, meaning the 8,000Hz benefit is strictly for PC competitive gaming.

The controller also offers four removable magnetic back buttons and two top claw-grip bumpers, with a modular magnetic design that lets players quickly swap components out, stripping the controller of unused buttons and extra weight. First-person shooter players can also use a back-mounted physical toggle switch with software-tunable actuation points, allowing them to fine-tune the hair-trigger click threshold.

That makes for a solid controller on paper, even if you don't need all of its features. The wireless model has an MSRP of $200, making it a little bit more expensive than the Xbox Elite Series 2 wireless controller and on par with the DualSense Edge (which can also be used on PC). If you'd prefer a wired option, the Wolverine V4 wired version will set you back $100.

Another controller worth keeping an eye on is the recently revealed Genki Manta. Genki launched a Kickstarter campaign for it, raising over $1.1 million for a peripheral that combines high customizability with an OLED display. The company aims to launch it next year, with an MSRP of $279.

title: Call Of Duty’s Richtofen Actor Wants Him To Come Back, Says 2027’s CoD Could Be From Sledgehammer
text:
Veteran video game actor Nolan North has addressed his future in the Call of Duty series, saying he hopes to reprise his character Dr. Edward Richtofen from Black Ops' popular Zombies mode.

If this does happen, it probably won't be soon. That's because, North said he believes 2027's Call of Duty game might be developed by Sledgehammer. Given that, a new Black Ops game might not come until 2028 at the soonest, but this is just conjecture.

Speaking at Gamergy in Puerto Rico (via DomTheBomb), North said he hopes Richtofen's story continues in a future Black Ops game, whenever that might be.

"I always like when they leave things open for the next one. I know that Infinity Ward and I think Sledgehammer has the next two before there is another Black Ops. I just don't want it to be the end of Richtofen, and I don't think it is," he said.

North clarified that he does not know for sure that Richotfen's story will continue, so he hoped people wouldn't think he had some inside knowledge apart from his own hope and belief. Whatever the case, North said Richotofen is one of his favorite characters to voice, and he hopes to reprise him someday.

North first appeared as Richtofen in 2008's World at War, and has reprised the role many times over in subsequent games from developer Treyarch. He's a fan-favorite character in the fan-favorite Zombies mode, with the story taking numerous twists and turns over the years.

"It's been such a pleasure getting to work with my friends for so long, just like Uncharted was," he said.

On the subject of Uncharted, North said he hopes to come back to play Nathan Drake once more. As it happens, rumors are swirling that Naughty Dog is working on Uncharted 5 and that Drake might have a role in it.

Regarding North's statement that Sledgehammer is working on the 2027 Call of Duty game, that's not confirmed, but doesn't seem outrageous given this has been reported since 2024. The studio's last game where it served as lead developer was 2023's Modern Warfare 3, so it might be time for Sledgehammer to take the lead again in 2027. Intriguingly, it's also been reported that Activision's new ownership of the Halo franchise could include Sledgehammer, or at least a division inside the developer, working on a Halo game.

This year's Call of Duty game is Modern Warfare 4, and Infinity Ward is leading development. The game releases on October 23 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC.

title: Solo Horror Dev Makes A Creepy Connection To A Real Haunted Island In Mexico
text:
Being a haunted doll must be difficult. You're missing an eyeball, and your lipstick makes you look more like a cannibal than a cherub. People make faces of disgust at you in the antique mall, and you want to tell them you're actually the unblemished soul of a 19th century nun named Eunice, but they speed away before you can. But if you were a haunted doll, you'd at least have solo developer Steelkrill Studio on your side, as its upcoming survival horror game Where Dolls Hang features real-life creepy dolls looking proudly injured. 

The dolls of Mexico's Isla de las Muñecas, the Island of the Dolls, have been through a lot over the past 80 years. Folklore suggests the bald dolls cobwebbed and nailed to the island's trees contain the spirit of a drowned little girl, who caretaker Don Julian Santana may or may not have made up. In any case, he spent much of his life fishing plastic Barbies and babies out of the water near his home to honor her spirit. So Where Dolls Hang, which was featured in the Horror Game Awards' recent showcase this past summer, is a tribute, too--it honors the fact that our real world is often freakier than fiction.

"Some of the doll models you'll find were created using real photographs," developer Steelkrill explains on Twitter. "The photographs can also be found around in the game." An accompanying clip of first-person gameplay footage demonstrates with an image of a doll head coated completely in dirt and little pimples from raindrops. The Where Dolls Hang player then drops the photo and stares ahead; the same pimply doll head is sticking from a pike right in front of them. 

"It creates an unusual connection between the game's horrors and reality: something disturbing hanging in a room or sitting in the darkness may not have been designed entirely from imagination," a press release says. "Somewhere in the world, there may be a real photograph behind it." Intriguingly, that makes Where Dolls Hang a rare game that is based on a true story, since life is unknowable without art to make sense of it. 

Where Dolls Hang is scheduled for a 2026 release date, and it's available to wishlist now on Steam.

title: GameStop Is Preparing Us For Next-Gen Pricing With $1,400 Used PS5 Pros
text:
Sticker shock might be underselling it with GameStop's new used pricing for Sony's most powerful system. Starting today, the video game store is listing pre-owned PS5 Pros for $1,400, though GameStop Pro members only need to dish out $1,330. Basically, it's a $500 surcharge over a brand-new PS5 Pro and capitalizing on the fact that those are stock-constrained currently.

A generous take on GameStop's new strategy for used PS5 Pros is that the company's conditioning us ahead of the possibility that the PS6 could cost $1,000 or more. Obviously, Sony isn't the only one increasing hardware pricing and consoles probably aren't getting cheaper anytime soon--mainly because of the ongoing chip shortage from AI development. 

A more cynical take is that GameStop is taking advantage of the situation similar to what scalpers do with the launch of new video game consoles. I'm also curious how many people now trade in a PS5 Pro at GameStop when they see how much the company is then reselling it for. Wouldn't an easier option just be to undercut them on Facebook Marketplace or eBay by $100? 

Similar pricing for used PS5 Pro systems can be seen on Amazon and Best Buy's storefronts. One key difference here is that those are third-party sellers, such as this RYTEK example at Best Buy. GameStop is officially behind the pre-owned pricing on its own website.

Sony raised pricing for PS5, PS5 Pro, and PlayStation Portal in April. The PS5 Pro was $750 previously and now retails for $900, if you can find one. When PS5 Pro originally launched in November 2024, the system cost $700. Meanwhile, the Xbox lineup also saw another round of price hikes in August, with the cheapest option being an Xbox Series S for $500. This is the first generation of video game systems to increase in price dramatically over the years, instead of getting much cheaper.

title: Warhammer Survivors Is Launching Mere Days Before GTA 6, And I Respect The Audacity
text:
The next Survivors-like game--or Survivaton, as Vampire Survivors developer Poncle refers to them--is out soon, and it's threatening to cut into GTA 6 playtime. Warhammer Survivors launches November 10 on PC, consoles, and mobile devices, and you can also grab a new demo on PC via Steam right now.

Set in the grim (and dark) 41st millennium of the Warhammer 40,000 franchise, Warhammer Survivors sticks to the Vampire Survivors playbook: You'll fight all manner of Tyranid enemies that threaten the Imperium of Man, evolve your weapons, and die a lot before you're strong enough to start easily tanking the waves of heretical creatures. Extremis bosses will push your builds to the limit, and when it launches, the game will feature over 40 playable characters and an arsenal of 70 weapons to collect.

Warhammer Survivors will release on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and Switch next month, and it'll also be available via Xbox Game Pass. The new demo will give you a fresh taste of the carnage, featuring the heroes Lyssa Revenya and the Legend of Catachan.

It's one of the few November games willing to take a risk and launch close to November 19, as many publishers and developers have opted to avoid the GTA 6-sized elephant in the room. Only a few games are standing their ground, including one that features the king of the monsters, Godzilla.

This isn't the only Survivaton on the way, as Poncle is also working on Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble. Like Vampire Survivors and Warhammer Survivors, it features the same bullet-heaven gameplay, but it draws from the manga and anime series' Culling Games storyline to shift the focus toward a "survivors royal" experience. The goal is to exorcise cursed spirits, grow your power, and outscore your opponents to be the last player standing. Originally scheduled to launch this year, the release date was shifted to 2027.

title: How To Get GTA 6’s $100 Edition For $80 Right Now
text:

GTA 6 becomes available to preload beginning November 12, and that applies to the game's digital and physical versions sold at retailers. The game unlocks to play on November 19 across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: Warner Bros. Games Now Belongs To Skydance, But Company Makes No Mention Of That In Big Announcement
text:
Paramount has officially completed its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, but the company's announcement of the deal closing did not contain a single mention of video games. That's notable because Warner Bros. Discovery is heavily invested in video games, and many may wonder what's coming next.

CEO David Ellison says he is a big gamer himself, but whether or not that means anything for the future of games at the new company, now known as Skydance, is unknown. Ellison, the son of billionaire Oracle founder Larry Ellison, courted controversy due to his family's dealings with Donald Trump and the current administration, with some industry observers believing the close relationship helped get the deal through the regulatory process.

Netflix originally secured the top bid for WBD and believed its deal would close, but Paramount swooped in with more money and a contract to buy the whole company, not just parts of it like Netflix was planning. For its part, Netflix executives spent time with Trump and his team as well. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos recently praised Trump for believing in and supporting the entertainment industry.

Skydance's press release announcing the closing of the deal hypes up Ellison's stated plans to put a minimum of 30 "high-quality" movies in theaters annually, and touts its "creative-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, and globally scaled" setup, but doesn't mention video games at all.

The news release does mention that the combined companies will offer content for people "across every entertainment vertical," and that would seemingly include video games. But the brief does not include any specifics. GameSpot has followed up with Skydance seeking more information.

Speaking to staff, Skydance boss Ynon Kreiz mentioned games specifically. According to The Hollywood Reporter, he said the company will have "plenty of opportunities to develop new businesses, products, games, and experiences to engage fans wherever they are and be where the consumer is going."

For what it's worth, when Netflix was planning to buy WBD, the streaming giant was similarly quiet on its plans for video games, saying it did not factor in video games very much. This came despite how 2023's Hogwarts Legacy was a bonafide juggernaut, selling more than 30 million copies.

While the release doesn't mention video games specifically, it does call out scary and tough times ahead for the people who work there. One of the main bullet points in the release was that Skydance is planning at least $6 billion in "run-rate syngeries within three years," which is likely a forecast for layoffs and cuts. Skydance's official word, however, is that the savings will "primarily" come from "technology, integration and procurement, marketing and real estate rationalization."

When big companies combine, layoffs often happen--it was the case for Microsoft, too, when it bought Activision Blizzard, with the company slashing thousands of jobs.

Skydance recently rolled out Paramount Games Studio, a team that folded in Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media. Projects in the works at those studios are continuing, including Marvel 1943: Rise of Hyrdra and a new Star Wars game with Lucasfilm from Amy Hennig, now under the Paramount Games Studio banner.

With Skydance now running the show, the company takes ownership of numerous big gaming properties, including Hogwarts Legacy developer Avalanche Software and its publishing label, Portkey Games; Mortal Kombat and its developer, NetherRealm; and Batman: Arkham studio Rocksteady. Skydance is also now in charge of Lego developer TT Games, and numerous other developers, including WB Games Boston, WB Games Montreal, WB Games New York, WB Games San Francisco, and numerous other studios.

Beyond developing games themselves, Skydance is making the Call of Duty movie with Activision, which is due for release in 2028.

title: Sega Announces $7,000 Sonic The Hedgehog Pottery, And I Can’t Stop Watching How It’s Made
text:
Time flies by fast, especially if you're Sega's blue mascot, as 2026 marks the 35th anniversary of Sonic the Hedgehog. While Sega has various plans to commemorate the milestone, one of the most elegant is a hand-painted porcelain sculpture that is both graceful and expensive. Even if you can afford to shell out big bucks for this Blue Blur pottery, you'll still need luck on your side, as only 50 of these pieces are being made.

Sculpted by the artisans of the Japanese studio YOYOYO, this ornate piece costs a whopping $7,000. It comes with a certificate of authenticity, a wooden stand, and a wooden box, but you'll need to enter a lottery to have a chance to buy it.

So what makes this piece so special? To realize the idea of Sonic being the "world's fastest blue," the studio incorporated gosu, a cobalt-blue underglaze pigment that results in a color that never fades. This created an "eternal blue" finish, and the artisans also designed this sculpture to have a shelf-life of at least 100 years.

For the base, durable Amakusa porcelain stone was chosen, as its white surface lets colors shine through, and the artists used techniques like delicate underglaze painting to create Seigaiha and Shippo patterns. This requires incredible skill and concentration to pull off successfully, as the patterns are ornate and hard to keep uniform. This is time-consuming, back-breaking work to do once, let alone 50 times, but the neat thing is that each piece will be unique up close, so you can appreciate the subtle details of the craft.

The red is also special, as it's applied to the partner piece that expresses the an endless infinity trail. According to the artists, glossy red carries motion and heat, and they also change expression with the viewing angle.

Other neat details include the other blue hues chosen for this project, with the Yagasuri shade featuring a stylized arrow-feather pattern to symbolize strong forward motion. You can take a closer look at how this work of Sonic the Hedgehog art was put together in the video above, which features a detailed (and enjoyably soothing) look at the artistry involved.

It might be a major anniversary year for Sonic the Hedgehog, but strangely, there's no game tie-in to mark the occasion. Sonic has had a consistent run of releases throughout the 2020s--with titles like Sonic Colors: Ultimate (2021), Sonic Frontiers (2022), Sonic Superstars (2023), Sonic X Shadow Generations (2024), and Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds (2025)--but it looks like the franchise is taking a break in 2026. While work continues on the next mainline game, Sega is leaning into updates for Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds alongside merchandise and community events to celebrate the decades-spanning career of its icon.

title: Steam Frame Gets VR Right Where So Many Others Went Wrong
text:
The virtual reality market has grown over the years, and depending on your budget, there's probably a VR headset out there for you. But can your VR gaming budget stretch to over $1,000 for the entry-level Steam Frame headset, and is it even worthwhile? That's the question GameSpot's senior video producer Kurt Indovina set out to answer, and after spending some time with it, his main takeaway was that it's the best VR headset he's ever used, and possibly the last one he'll ever own.

"Having used this solid piece of tech for a couple of weeks now, it's been great to replay things like Half-Life: Alyx or booting up Ghost Town, or fiddling around in Hot Dogs, Horseshoes, and Hand Grenades," Indovina explained. "It's also been a time of reflection for VR as a whole, from where it started, where it went, and where it currently sits now. I've been an advocate for VR for a while. I've made plenty of videos about VR. In fact, the first GameSpot video I ever appeared in was for Five Nights at Freddy's VR."

"But for all of the love I've given VR, my gripes with it seem to be never-ending. I've been very vocal about how companies have stunted the growth of VR and are trying to chokehold the market with their product. Meta putting out the most affordable and accessible headset only to commit, for lack of a better term, public suicide by investing everything into the metaverse, favoring a dystopian weird social life and alienating people who just want to play games."

But if you look at the Steam Frame in a vacuum? "It rules," Indovina said. "I'm sure this thing will get support for a lot of other cool games. It's great."

The Steam Frame isn't the first time that Valve has launched VR hardware, but compared to 2019's Valve Index, this standalone wireless headset is a major leap forward. It offers inside-out tracking, improved streaming support, onboard processing, and Android compatibility, but it is one of the pricier models on the market right now. It's still cheaper than Meta's next foray into virtual reality, as the Facebook parent company recently unveiled its new $1,300 Meta VR Glasses, with a flashy trailer that didn't even mention VR gaming.

But if you've got the cash to flash and you're purely interested in gaming, the Steam Frame is worth considering, if you can get your hands on one, since they've sold out surprisingly fast. If you wear glasses, you'll also want to double-check your frame and avoid making an expensive purchase for high-tech VR gear you can't use.

title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Is Free To Play Now, If You Know Where To Look
text:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is finally out, and so far, it might just be one of the best Star Wars games ever made. The new racing game has an attractive MSRP of $60, but if you're looking to grab it for the low price of nothing, you can play it for free through Amazon Luna starting today.

Amazon has announced that Prime members can stream the single-player campaign for free through Amazon Luna. "We've always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” Jeff Gattis, Head of Gaming at Amazon, said in a blog post. "Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. It's exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think players are going to love it."

If you're unfamiliar with it, Amazon Luna is a cloud gaming service and platform available to Prime members. A rotating selection of games appears every month through Luna, and members can also claim several downloadable PC games. These can be redeemed through storefronts like the Epic Games Store and GOG. Last month was particularly good, as members could claim several of id Software's critically acclaimed Doom games, including the 2016 reboot and Doom Eternal.

Set early during the era of the New Republic, Star Wars: Galactic Racer follows players as they take part in the Galactic League, a high-stakes underground racing circuit. What sets the game apart from other racing titles is its roguelike gameplay mechanics, which evolve the standard racing formula into a dynamic experience. Developed by Fuse Games--a studio founded by racing veterans from the Burnout and Need for Speed franchises--Star Wars: Galactic Racer currently has a metascore of 88 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic.

"Galactic Racer is those absolutely perfect 10 minutes expanded into a full game. Every moment feels joyfully fast," Jordan Ramée wrote in GameSpot's Star Wars: Galactic Racer review. "Every decision carries the weight of tension. And every run is a rewarding chance to learn, improve, tinker, and adapt, whether it ends in success or failure. I can’t wait to keep playing what’s been my favorite racing game in years."

title: Halloween’s First DLC Reveals Even The Bad Sequels Will Get Some Love
text:
Halloween's first paid DLC is coming on October 27 in the form of a new skin for the game's killer, Michael Myers, and it's pulling from a source you might not expect: Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers. A free update on the same day will also add a fifth map, The Tower Farm, inspired by a location in the same film. 

It may seem odd to jump to the fifth movie for the game's first DLC, but it's not the only piece of new content coming that day. There's also a second skin coming for Big Mike, borrowing from his look in the legacy sequel Halloween (2018). Each skin will run you $10.

Survivor mains also have new things to look forward to, including two new characters, Michelle and Eugene, as well as Civilian Costumes Pack 1, which includes 14 outfits--one for each survivor character--and 42 colorings, or "tints." The new survivors will also go for $10, though that's for the pair, not for each of them, while the new styles and colors will be--you guessed it--$10 for the set. This content drop is the first of several coming to the game in its first year, development studio Illfonic said. 

With 13 movies in the series, there's still plenty of ground to cover for Halloween, which makes kicking off its post-launch roadmap with Halloween 5 such an interesting choice. The appropriately autumnal farm map is more open than the game's earlier maps, making it harder to break line of sight from Haddonfield's boogeyman. I suppose that moody setting was too picturesque to pass up as an update just days before October 31. 

As much as I love the 1978 original, I'm not particularly fond of most of the Halloween sequels, though Halloween H20 is probably dearest to me; I fondly recall seeing it on the big screen as a horror-obsessed nine-year-old, so I look forward to seeing that one reflected in the game down the line.

In any event, I don't think the sequels' quality ought to keep the development team from bringing them into the game like this. Illfonic's game should be a museum to all things Halloween, and watching it become that over the next few years is an exciting prospect. I hope the licensing deal extends to the series' more oddball entries, like Rob Zombie's reboot duology and Halloween 3--the one movie in the series that doesn't involve Michael Myers. If the game follows the roadmap I've built in my mind, we'll see every version of The Shape on the character select screen one day.

In GameSpot's Halloween review, I wrote that it gives players "a vibes-heavy experience befitting the timeless film, while also offering a unique hook that keeps the game from feeling like a rehash of the many horror multiplayer games that came before it."

title: Uncharted 5: Everything We Know About The Unconfirmed Game
text:
Naughty Dog's Uncharted series sold millions of copies, got solid reviews, and was spun off into a movie starring Spider-Man actor Tom Holland--however, the game franchise has been dormant for years. Fans are wondering if Naughty Dog will return to its Indiana Jones-style action-adventure series, and while that remains to be seen, there have been clues about the future of the Uncharted series.

There are no guarantees that Uncharted 5 will ever happen, but there is a chance. Here is everything we've heard so far about the next Uncharted game.

In This Article
  • "Never say never"
  • A cryptic photo
  • 2026 rumors
  • What else is Naughty Dog working on?
  • A different studio could make Uncharted 5
  • "There's no story left for us to tell"
  • "Some planning" for Uncharted 5
  • Naughty Dog chooses what it makes based on passion
  • Naughty Dog has released nothing "new" on PS5 so far
  • All the Uncharted games so far
  • When could we learn more?
  • What about the next Uncharted movie?

"Never say never"

In 2022, Shaun Escayg, a Naughty Dog veteran who worked on Uncharted 4 and The Lost Legacy, said in an interview with GamesRadar that the team has a "never say never" attitude about making Uncharted 5. Uncharted 4 may have wrapped up series hero Nathan Drake's story, but that doesn't necessarily put a cap on where the franchise could go.

"I think we can say for certain that we can never say never. Yeah. Uncharted is a franchise we love--that the studio loves. It's a world we want to see more of. So I can certainly say that," Escayg said.

A cryptic photo

Escayg, in February of 2026, posted a vague Instagram photo of a cannon in a tropical environment that was captioned "research." People are theorizing that Escayg went to Fort George at Trinidad and Tobago to help research a new Uncharted game. It's rumored that merchants stored records and valuables at Fort George, further fueling the connection to Uncharted.

Nothing is certain, of course, and Escayg might have been referencing pretty much anything with his post, or nothing at all.

2026 rumors

Most recently, multiple reports said Naughty Dog is making a new Uncharted game, and it's not another remake. Instead, it's said to be a new game, and that Nathan Drake actor Nolan North could appear in some manner.

For his part, North said he's definitely game to come back, if he's asked.

“110%. Absolutely. I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it. It just depends if Sony wants to make money,” he said at Gamergy in Puerto Rico prior to the recent rumors of Uncharted 5 (via DomTheBomb). “I absolutely would. I try to stay in shape just in case. I can’t see a scenario where I would say no. I always keep out hope.”

I

What else is Naughty Dog working on?

After cancelling The Last of Us Online in 2023, Naughty Dog said it had two single-player games in development. One is the new IP Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and the other remains a mystery. Some believe it could be The Last of Us: Part III, which Naughty Dog has seemingly teased time and again over the years. Others contend it could be a new Uncharted game.

A different studio could make Uncharted 5

If a fifth mainline Uncharted game is in the works, that doesn't necessarily mean Naughty Dog will make it. Studio head Neil Druckmann previously said Uncharted 5 could happen with a different developer. Naughty Dog would assist an outside studio to help make sure whatever team made a hypothetical new Uncharted game would get the "essence" right, Druckmann explained.

"There's no story left for us to tell"

In 2016, just ahead of Uncharted 4's release, Druckmann told GameSpot that there was no guarantee that Naughty Dog would leave Uncharted behind forever, but he sounded pretty sure that would be the case. "There's no story left for us to tell," Druckmann said.

"Looking at the three games as setup, Uncharted 4 is the payoff," he elaborated. "If we're telling these stories honestly, and we're being honest with who these characters are, then we have to say, 'This is it, there's nothing else left to tell with this character. This is how it ends, and there's nothing to go on after that.'"

Dovetailing with the above mention of how another studio could make a new Uncharted game, Druckmann told us in 2016 that someone could pitch Naughty Dog on a prequel and the studio might agree to that.

Beyond the possibility of a prequel, some fans are wondering if a fifth game could take place after the events of Uncharted 4 and be told through the lens of Cassie, the daughter of Nathan Drake and Elena. In fact, the epilogue of Uncharted 4 had players playing as Cassie, walking through their home and discovering some of her father's artifacts that he himself found on his many journeys.

The previous Uncharted games told Nathan Drake's story, and 2017's The Lost Legacy told a story from Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross' perspective.

"Some planning" for Uncharted 5

According to Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming, there was "some planning of an Uncharted 5" prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. Henderson didn't have any further details about these apparently plans or what the story for a fifth Uncharted game might be--only that the idea was kicked around in some manner. That only makes sense from a business and planning perspective, of course. The Uncharted series is well-known, has passionate fans, and has been dormant for a while, making it a potential prime candidate for a new entry to appeal to fans and create new ones.

Naughty Dog chooses what it makes based on passion

Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann said in 2023 that he feels lucky that studio owner Sony trusts the company enough to allow Druckmann and other key decision-makers to choose what they make next. He said at the end of every project, "We purposefully explore several different projects" for what comes next. "Some of them might be a sequel, and then a bunch of new ideas. And then we feel like, 'Where do our passions lie?'"

Giving Naughty Dog the freedom to choose its own projects makes sense. After all, Naughty Dog has delivered hit after hit for Sony, presumably earning them respect and reputation. At the same time, of course Sony management would be involved in some capacity in meetings about what comes next. A variety of perspectives are no doubt calculated when Naughty Dog sets out to make a new game.

Naughty Dog has released nothing "new" on PS5 so far

Naughty Dog has not released a "new" game during the PS5 generation. The Last of Us: Part II was released in 2020 for PS4 but didn't come to PS5 until 2024 in the form of a remaster, of sorts. There was also 2022's The Last of Us Part I, a remake of the 2013 game for PS5. A remastered version of The Last of Us: Part II was released for PS5 in January 2024. These are technically "new" games, but they are not brand-new games. Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is expected to be Naughty Dog's first all-new game for PS5, but it's not scheduled to release until 2027 at the soonest.

All the Uncharted games so far

There have been four mainline Uncharted games released since the franchise debuted in 2007, in addition to 2017's standalone spin-off Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, which focused on Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross.

Here is a rundown of all 10 Uncharted games to date.

  • Uncharted: Drake's Fortune (2007) - Developed by Naughty Dog and released on PS3
  • Uncharted 2: Among Thieves (2009) - Developed by Naughty Dog and released on PS3
  • Uncharted: Drake's Deception (2011) - Developed by Naughty Dog and released on PS3
  • Uncharted: Golden Abyss (2011) - Developed by Bend Studio and released on PlayStation Vita
  • Uncharted: Fight for Fortune (2012) - Developed by Bend Studio and released on PlayStation Vita
  • Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection (2015) - Developed by Bluepoint Games and released on PS4
  • Uncharted 4: A Thief's End (2016) - Developed by Naughty Dog and released on PS4
  • Uncharted: Fortune Hunter (2016) - Developed by Playspree and released on iOS and Android
  • Uncharted: The Lost Legacy (2017) - Developed by Naughty Dog and released on PS4
  • Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection (2022) - Developed by Iron Galaxy and released on PS5 and PC

When could we learn more?

There is no indication that Uncharted 5 is real, let alone when it could be announced. That being said, Sony could announce it during one of its State of Play or PlayStation Showcase events, whenever the next one might be. Keep checking back with GameSpot for the latest.

What about the next Uncharted movie?

Beyond the games, an Uncharted movie starring Tom Holland was released in 2022. It made more than $400 million worldwide, and is the No. 8 highest-grossing video game movie of all time. Studio Sony Pictures said Uncharted could become a film "franchise," but no new movies have been announced.

title: Amid Uncharted 5 Rumors, Nathan Drake Actor Says He Would Come Back, But With One Catch
text:
One of actor Nolan North's most famous roles is that of Nathan Drake in Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise, but he wrapped things up with 2016's Uncharted 4: A Thief's End. There are rumors that Naughty Dog is making a new Uncharted game, and North has said he would "110%" be up for coming back in a new game in the storied series.

“110%. Absolutely. I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it. It just depends if Sony wants to make money," he said at Gamergy in Puerto Rico prior to the recent rumors of Uncharted 5 (via DomTheBomb). "I absolutely would. I try to stay in shape just in case. I can't see a scenario where I would say no. I always keep out hope."

North went on to clarify that he has not heard anything about a new Uncharted game where he might be asked to come back, but he thinks it would be a good business decision for Sony.

"It is a business-my god, can you imagine if they did? It would be the biggest announcement in gaming. I don't think that's hyperbole. I think that's true," he said.

North said he enjoyed working with Naughty Dog over the years on the four main Uncharted games, and that's part of why he would be up to come back.

His one caveat, however, is that he hopes Naughty Dog wouldn't make something that doesn't live up to the franchise's legacy. He cited Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull as an example of a middling movie in an otherwise great series, and he doesn't want that to happen for Uncharted.

According to multiple sources, a fifth mainline Uncharted game will be Naughty Dog's next project after Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, which is reportedly due for release in 2027. A third The Last of Us game could follow after.

Intriguingly, the report said Nathan Drake would appear in the hypothetical Uncharted 5 in some capacity. Uncharted 4 was positioned as the definitive end for Nathan Drake’s story when it released in 2016, but Naughty Dog has repeatedly suggested that it is not done with the franchise. 

When Uncharted 5 might release is anyone’s guess, but it’s more likely that it’ll arrive on the PlayStation 6 given that Sony is expected to release its next-generation console sometime in 2028. 

North played Nathan Drake in the four main Uncharted games, but not The Lost Legacy. He had a cameo in the Uncharted movie, too.

title: New Gears Of War: E-Day Patch Addresses Giant Vomiting Frog Error Codes
text:
Gears of War: E-Day rolls out worldwide starting October 6, and thanks to early access players, The Coalition has identified several issues that it's fixing with the game's first patch. Focused mostly on overall stability and performance across the game's campaign, multiplayer, and Horde Siege modes, the Gears of War: E-Day update is out now.

One of the biggest fixes is the "Bilefrog-Kalona" error, an issue named after the gigantic subterranean Locust frogs encountered throughout the game, which regularly try to kill you by vomiting stomach acid at your position. Nasty stuff. The Coalition assigned several Gears-themed names to its network errors, and in this case, getting vomit-frogged is a specific split-screen multiplayer issue. This triggers when a split-screen player is automatically signed out of online services after the console or PC is suspended, then tries to use Quick Resume to hop back in.

The Coalition says it has also addressed an issue in Versus Social matches that results in players entering a waiting-lobby limbo, and fixed an issue that could prevent certain Siege Blitz Secure objectives from being completed. For the campaign, several pesky problems across Act 2 are being patched, while other game-wide instances of sticky turrets and unearned War Journal progress have been resolved.

These fixes come on the eve of the game's worldwide rollout on PC and Xbox Series X|S, and an influx of Game Pass subscribers are expected to enter Kalona starting tomorrow. While the overall story isn't the best Gears of War narrative, the game is still recommended for anyone who wants a big, dumb, and loud cover-based shooter that looks gorgeous on PC and Xbox Series X|S.

"For better or worse, E-Day is distinctly Gears, and I had a good time with it, even if the story is disappointing and the open areas are fairly dull," Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot's Gears of War: E-Day campaign review. "But that’s all it is: a good game, propped up by combat that hasn’t changed all that much over the past 20 years. That’s enough to skate by, but I wish Gears of War would dig deeper."

Gears of War: E-Day October 5 Patch Notes

Stability and Performance

  • Made various stability, performance, hardware compatibility, and reporting improvements across the game

Online and multiplayer services

  • Addressed an issue causing some Versus Social matches to remain on the “Waiting for players” screen
  • Improved Xbox authentication handling when the system clock differs significantly from the correct time
  • Addressed "Bilefrog-Kalona" error, where a split-screen player could be signed out after suspending and resuming the game
  • Improved online-session stability when accessing session information

Campaign

  • Addressed an issue where players joining an existing Campaign could receive War Journal progress and Forge rewards earned before they joined
  • Addressed an issue where players could remain attached to turrets when a cinematic or gameplay moment began
  • Addressed an issue where some join-in-progress players might not receive the expected Forge Discovery War Journal progress
  • Act 2 Chapter 2: Addressed an issue where the objective could fail to update when entering Allfather’s Plaza after completing activities elsewhere in the mission
  • Act 2 Chapter 2: Addressed an issue where the Heavy Gear in the Black Raven Down side objective could appear without a Vulcan
  • Act 4 Chapter 1: Addressed an issue where certain side objectives could fail to start if players entered the objective area while introductory dialogue was playing
  • Act 4 Chapter 2: Addressed one cause of the Power Station defense objective failing to complete after all visible enemies were defeated

Horde Siege

  • Addressed an issue that could prevent certain Siege Blitz Secure objectives from being completed
  • Addressed an issue where the extraction helicopter could fail to appear during a Downtown West Blitz mission

Versus

  • Addressed an issue in Demolition where a bomb could become stuck in a defusing state if a player was eliminated while beginning the defuse interaction

UI

  • Adjusted the size and appearance of Online Diagnostic text
  • Addressed one possible cause of the UI repeatedly attempting to claim the same Challenge Mail reward

title: Why GTA Studio Co-Founder Is Avoiding GTA 6–And All Open-World Games
text:
Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser left the company in 2020 and now runs a new outfit called Absurd Ventures. Houser will be forever connected to the GTA franchise, and he's now weighed in on GTA 6.

He told Variety that he did not watch the "Extended Look" trailer and doesn't plan to. Why? He said he tries to avoid consuming things that are going to "disrupt me creatively."

"And given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he said. "I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently.”

Also in the interview, Houser said he doesn't play a lot of open-world games anymore, for similar reasons.

"I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature,'" he said. "I’m not a game designer; I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about.”

It's not that Absurd Ventures is burying its head in the sand, however. Houser went on to say he has a team of people at his company who take the time to examine "what everyone else is doing."

He said when Rockstar began to develop Red Dead Redemption, he avoided watching any more Western films. For GTA, he said he avoided HBO's acclaimed mob show The Sopranos (1999-2007) because "it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA" if he had seen the show while formulating the GTA series, which was first released in 1997.

"So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me," he said.

Houser is now working on multiple projects at Absurd Ventures, including an open-world comedy game that he will reveal further "in the next few months." Another is a dystopian sci-fi game about "video game development gone very wrong" when a rogue AI becomes sentient.

He said in the Variety interview that "there could be no greater compliment" than to be forever associated with GTA. At the same time, Houser said he hopes some of what he works on at Absurd Venture can be successful in its own right.

Dan Houser's brother and Rockstar co-founder, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and was involved in the creation of GTA 6. GQ writer Sam White recently posted a series of tweets (and then deleted them) saying an interview he had planned with Sam Houser fell apart at the last minute. That's notable because Sam Houser rarely gives any interviews at all, nor does he appear in Rockstar's official promotional efforts for the company's releases.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. In other news, Rockstar recently revealed some of its secrets and detailed how a game like GTA 6 gets made.

title: Hideo Kojima Is Keeping OD A Mystery To Make Its Horror Hit Harder
text:
Games developed by Hideo Kojima typically have an air of mystery, but for his upcoming horror project OD, the veteran game director wants to both terrify and mystify his fans. On a new episode of his weekly radio show Koji10, Kojima briefly spoke about the game, avoiding the release of teasers, and ensuring that players get a proper shock when playing it

"It's still a mystery. That doesn't mean we haven't made the game," Kojima said. "I want to keep quiet and release it. That's unusual for me, isn't it? I normally put out teaser after teaser. This time I don't want to reveal much. A mystery. It's so new that it's a mystery. It aims to create a new experience and test the limits of what players can bear in terms of fear. The limits of fear, that's the idea behind the title. The critical point of fear."

OD was originally announced in 2023, with the game being described as an experiment on what it means to overdose on fear--hence the title, OD. As for Kojima's comments about marketing, the first Death Stranding was a prime example: There were several teaser trailers and extended gameplay previews, each leaving viewers with more questions than answers. Kojima isn't even sure OD will find an audience, as he believes the gameplay systems are unlike anything he's created in his career.

Alongside his Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint, Xbox is supporting development on OD, and the game is reportedly safe from the studio closures, layoffs, and game cancellations that have hit Microsoft's gaming division throughout 2026.

The game features actors Hunter Schafer and Sophia Lillis, although it's unclear how much of a role the late Udo Kier will have in OD, following his death last year. Kojima previously said that the 2025 SAG-AFTRA strike forced the team to reschedule filming for OD until 2026, although Kier can still be seen in the early teaser for OD.
